steps.label: Divide above and below by x
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both the numerator and the denominator are 0 at x = 0, so neither is a standard limit on its own. Dividing both by x makes each one a standard limit.
lines: For x ≠ 0 divide the numerator and the denominator by x.

steps.why: The denominator is also 0 at x = 0, so this is a ratio of two 0/0 pieces. Dividing each by x is what turns them into the two standard limits the syllabus states, and each of those has a known value.
common_mistakes: Treating the denominator as a constant and using only lim (3ˣ − 1)/x = logₑ3.
Dividing only the numerator by x and forgetting the denominator.
steps.memory_tip: When the top and the bottom are both 0, divide both by x. Each half then becomes one of the standard limits you already know.

steps.label: Take the ratio of the two standard limits
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both limits exist and the lower one, 1/2, is not 0, so the limit of the quotient is the quotient of the limits. Dividing by 1/2 is multiplying by 2.
lines: Both limits exist and the denominator limit 1/2 is not 0,
so the limit of the quotient is the quotient of the limits.

recall.must_convey: That the answer is logₑ3 divided by 1/2, that is 2 logₑ3.
accept: log three divided by half gives two log three
the answer is two log three

steps.why: The quotient rule for limits needs both limits to exist and the lower one to be non-zero, and both conditions hold here. The value checks numerically: at x = 0.00001 the expression is 2.19724, and 2 logₑ3 = 2.19722.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by 1/2 instead of dividing by it, giving (logₑ3)/2.
Writing logₑ9 as 2 by confusing it with log₃9 = 2; logₑ9 = 2 logₑ3 ≈ 2.197 is the exact answer.
steps.memory_tip: Dividing by 1/2 doubles the number. So the answer is twice logₑ3, and 2 logₑ3 = logₑ9 by the power rule for logarithms.
lines_compact: Both limits exist and the denominator limit 1/2 is not 0,
so the limit of the quotient is the quotient of the limits.

insider_note: Divide top and bottom by x so BOTH become standard limits: (aˣ − 1)/x → logₑa and (√(1+x) − 1)/x → 1/2. Dividing by a half doubles, so the answer is 2logₑ3 = logₑ9.
